column1: # Safety mutants of the gz read side: gzread, gzfread, gzgetc, gzungetc (script rows, gz-read.py, which makes
# the same edit in each rfl restatement of the code so that only a semantic lemma can fail) and gzclose_r (plain
# rows: its proofs run the translation directly). Each row drops a refusal, skips a free or a call that frees,
# or moves a bound by one, outside loop bodies. Every row but gzclose_r-return-value breaks a clause of
# GzCallSafe or GzCloseSafe (no fault, the caller regions, the ledger, the invariant) on a permitted input;
# gzclose_r-return-value is caught by the exact run lemma (run_buf), not by a safety clause.
# A skipped gz_error or a wrong return value of gzread, gzfread, gzgetc and gzungetc is not a row: the safety
# statement does not observe it (no block is allocated or freed), so only a restatement could fail.
# The rows marked "pending" are for gzgets and gzdirect, whose proofs are not on dev; the module names are
# placeholders. Uncomment them when the proofs land.
